newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iraqi Kurds abandon peace talks after killing.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi Kurds abandon peace talks after killing.

text.p: A Kurdish group on Tuesday walked out of Western-sponsored talks trying to end rivaly between Iraqi Kurdish factions because of the killing of one of its members.
"On receiving the news of the killing of our colleague...we left the meeting," Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) leading member Sami Abdurrahman told a news conference.

He accused the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) of killing Muhittin Rahim, head of the KDP in the Iraqi town of Halabja. "All indications show the PUK is directly involved and responsible for this act of terror."
The two groups have met frequently in Ankara since they declared a ceasefire last year after weeks of fighting. The United States, Turkey and Britain are sponsoring the talks.

The KDP, led by Massoud Barzani, used Iraqi troops and tanks to take the key city of Arbil from its rival last August. The United States fired missiles at southern Iraq in response to Baghdad's involvement.
Abdurrahman did not say when and where the killing happened but said his group would not attend further talks until it was cleared up.
"The KDP will not attend any other meeting of this sort until a thorough investigation is carried out under the sponsorship of the peacemakers and the results are declared," he said.
